chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Amriki from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) said:

I asked him about a man, is it suitable for him to lead prayer in sarawil (trousers) and qalansawah (cap)? He said, 'It is not suitable.' And I asked him about the sarawil, is it permissible in place of the izar (loincloth)? He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.الإِزَارِ: The loincloth or lower garment traditionally worn by men, often wrapped around the waist.
key_terms.سَرَاوِيلَ: Trousers or pants, a lower garment covering the legs.
key_terms.قَلَنْسُوَةٍ: A cap or skullcap worn on the head.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to lead prayer wearing trousers and a cap according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Musa al-Kazim clarifies the distinction between the legal validity (jawaaz) and the recommended propriety (istihbaab) of prayer attire, noting that while trousers are a valid substitute for the traditional izar, they are not ideal for leading prayer. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that permissible clothing does not automatically equate to the preferred attire for the imam, emphasizing modesty and dignity in worship. The ruling underscores the flexibility in adapting traditional garments to contemporary contexts while maintaining spiritual decorum.
